title: Reading a complete configuration record
statement: Let $k$ be natural, let $Q,T,S$ be types with decidable equality, let $M$ be a $k$-tape Boolean Turing machine, let $u:T\times\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\to T$, let $N$ be a two-tape Boolean machine with fixed states $s_0,s_1\in S$, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. For a natural number $s$, a configuration $c$ of $M$, a tag $\tau\in T$, and a four-tape record-machine configuration $d$, assume every work-tape head of $c$ lies within distance $s$ of zero and every tape cell outside that window is blank; assume that $d$ records the full configuration record formed from $c$ and $\tau$ on tape 0, and that all other tapes of $d$ are blank. Then the record machine reaches the snapshot whose control is the read-exit control associated with the data read from $c$ (with tag $\tau$), and whose tapes 1 and 3 each hold the encoded binary input-position digits, within $(10(k+3)+17)(L+1)$ steps, where $L$ is the length of the joined configuration record and each work-tape head stays within distance $L+1$ of its initial position. The run avoids both verdict states before its final time.
hypotheses_covered: fixed start and finish states in $S$
$c$'s work heads lie within radius $s$ and cells outside the window are blank
$d$ records the encoded full configuration and tag
all nonzero-indexed tapes of $d$ are blank
caveat: The private record relation and snapshot specify the detailed layout; the prose summarizes the requested read result and run bounds.
